Emergency fund stays intact (¥3,000). Coach Liu emphasized this: "You never know when you'll need immediate cash for injury treatment or unexpected travel. Don't spend your buffer on equipment that can be funded through institutional channels."

They're actually helpful filters:
- Team allowance excludes monitoring devices → tells me this is expected personal investment
- Subsidy can't overlap with team allowance → forces efficient allocation across channels
- Sponsorship limited to branded items → ensures I use it before expiration

- Competing priorities: injury treatment vs. performance optimization
- Emotional factors: fear of injury, desire for competitive edge
- Difficult trade-offs: immediate pain relief vs. long-term investment

title: Equipment Defect Crisis - Decision Framework Analysis

- Manufacturer taking responsibility
Cons:

- 200+ training hours of familiarity
- Mental certainty - can focus 100% on race strategy
- Previous personal bests achieved in this model

- Lose 2850 CNY investment (sunk cost)

- Psychological feeling of 'not having the best'

Option 3: Emergency Repair
Pros:
- Keep the custom equipment I paid for
- Potentially save the 2850 CNY investment
- Get the theoretical performance advantage
Cons:
- Unknown structural integrity under max competition force
- HIGH injury risk (ankle, Achilles, knee) - could END Olympic qualification campaign
- Psychological uncertainty during race
- Repair cost ~500-800 CNY (estimated)

Priority 3: Performance optimization
Priority 4: Financial recovery

TEAMMMATE ZHANG'S EXPERIENCE: Tried emergency replacement last year, arrived too late, borrowed ill-fitting equipment, performed poorly. Mental stress of uncertainty worse than equipment difference.
